5. After the aforesaid judgment of the Supreme Court Khorshed Alam worked officially as mutwalli for the period from 19.6.68. Since Khorshed Alam did not file any suit about his parantage in pursuance of the judgment of the Supreme Court, the present petitioner filed a suit being O.C. Suit No.457 of 1977 in the Court of Sadar Munsif, Rajshahi, against the opposite party No. 1 praying for a decree declaring to the effect that the defendant No. 1 Khorshed Alam is a child of some unknown parentage other than that of late Amir Ali Mia and for a decree declaring that the plaintiff is the only eligible person to be appointed as Mutwalli of the Salamat Mia Waqf Estate enrolled under E.C. No.4028 of Rajshahi in terms of the Waqf deed itself. The opposite-party Khorshed Alam contested the suit and ultimately the suit was decreed on 30.11.79 by a judgment of the learned Munsif who held that defendant No. 1 Khorshed Alam alias Shaha Alam, the son of some unknown parentage other than that of late Amir Ali Mia, it was declared that the plaintiff Amir Sultan Ali Haider, the eldest son of late Amir Ali Mia, is the only eligible person to be appointed as Mutwali of Salamat Mia Waqf Estate according to the terms and conditions of the Waqf deed. After the aforesaid judgment and decree, the present petitioner Amir Sultan Ali Haider was appointed as Mutwalli of the aforesaid waqf estate on 22.12.79, but he Got charge on 11.8.81 through the Deputy go Commissioner, Rajshahi, and since then he was performing his functions as Mutwalli of the aforesaid waqf estate. 

 6. The opposite-party Khorshed Alam fill O.C. Appeal No. 117 of 1979 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Rajshahi, against the judgment and decree passed in O.C. Suit No.457 of 1977 by the Munsif. The learned District Judge disallowed the appeal on contest on 10.12.81. Thereafter, the opposite-party Khorshed Alam filed Civil Revision No.263 of 1981 in the High Court Division challenging the judgment and decree passed in O.C. Appeal No. 117 of 1979. The aforesaid Rule issued in Civil Revision case was discharged on 5.5.81 and the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court was affirmed. Again opposite party Khorshed Alam preferred an appeal before the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh against the judgment and decree of the High Court Division being Civil Appeal No,68 of 1983. The aforesaid civil appeal was disposed of on 22.3.84 whereby majority view of their Lordships of the Supreme Court, Appellate Division, the Judgment and decree passed by the Courts below were set aside and the opposite-party Khorshed Alam was declared as the legal son of late Amir Ali Mia. But their Lordships held in respect of second prayer in O.C. Suit No.457 of 1977 regarding eligibility of appointing a Mutwalli of the aforesaid waqf cstate that "since the prayer No. 1 that the defendant No. 1 Md. Khorshed Alam is the child of some unknown parentage other than that of Md. Amir Ali Mia cannot be granted in view of the proposition of law mentioned above, the 2nd prayer does not come for consideration inasmuch as the conditions for appointment of Mutwalli are mentioned in the waqf deed itself and it is for the statutory functionary namely, the Administrator of Waqfs, to consider whether thos conditions have been fulfilled by any individual." 

 8. In the order of the Waqf Administrator dated 21.12.86, it appears that he had taken pains to discuss all the facts and circumstances of the case. It appears that the parties were duly notified and this opposite-party No. 1 Khorshed Alam appeared and filed his written objection before the Administrator of Waqfs. The Administrator of Waqfs in his order, considered the facts and circumstances the conduct of opposite party No.1 Khorshed Alam and his performance as Mutwalli for the period from 19.6.87 to the matter was also inquired into by the inspector concerned who submitted a report. The Administrator of Waqfs also sought report from the local police administration of the district of Rajshahi and he got the report and considered it. After considering the materials on record, he found that there were allegations against opposite-party No.1 Khorshed Alam made during the Mutwilliship of late Amir Ali Mia. During the Mutwilliship of late Amir Ali Mia, Khorshed Alain was a lesee in the waqf property and he individually defaulted in paying monthly rent to the estate and as such Amir Ali Mia as Mutwalli instituted Money Suit No.30 of 1985 for realization of arrear rents. The suit was decreed oil contest. As the monthly tenant Khorshed Alain had damaged the waqf estate and acted against the interest of waqf estate, the former Mutwalli Amir Ali Mia had instituted O.C. Suit No.381 of 1966 in the Court of Sadar Munsif, Rajshahi, for eviction of Khorshed Alam from the premises and that suit was decreed against Khorshed Alam, another complaint was lodged against Khorshed Alam in Sutrapur Police Station at Dhaka (F.I.R. No.72 dated 5.9.72 under Section 170/420 of the B.P.C.) and Khorshed Alam was taken into custody and he remained in jail for about six months. 

 12. There is another finding of the learned Additional District Judge to the effect that the provisions of Section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance had not been complied with. From the record it appears that after the judgment passed by the Appellate Division in Civil Appeal No. 27 of 1975, Khorshed Alam was made Mutwalli on 19.6.78 and he contiuned upto 11.8.81. In the judgment of the Appellate Division Khorshed Alam was directed to tile a suit for determination of his parentage. But Khorshed Alam did not file any suit. Ultimately, the present petitioner Amir Suhan Ali Haider filed the suit being O.C. Suit No. 457 of 1977, for a declaration that Khorshed Alam was not the legal and legitimate son of Amir Ali Mia. In that suit the petitioner Amir Sultan Ali Haider obtained a decree and after obtaining that decree in O.C. Suit No.457 of 1977, Amir Sultan Ali Haider was again made Mutwalli and he took charge of office of the Mutwalli of the said Waqf Estate on 11.8.81 and since then he was discharging his functions as Mutwalli of the said Waqf Estate. The trial court, in O.C. Suit No.457 of 1977, held that Khorshed Alam was not the legitimate son of Amir Ali Mia which was affirmed by the lower appellate Court as well as by the High Court Division. On appeal before the Appellate Division in Civil Appeal No.68 of 1983, the judgment of the Courts below were set-aside and the Appellate Division held that Khorshed Alam is the legitimate son of late Amir Ali Mia. As regards appointment of Mutwalli, the Appellate Division held that it would be done by the Administrator of Waqf in accordance with the terms of waqf deed and the provisions of Waqfs Ordinance. Under this circumstance this Amir Sultan Ali Haider filed an application on 11.5.85 before the Administrator of Waqf for appointement of a Mutwalli on regular basis in pursuance of the judgment of the Appellate Division. But the fact remains that Amir Sultan Ali Haider was discharging his functions as Mutwalli since 11.8.81 in pursuance of the decree passed in O.C. Suit No.457 of 1977. It appears to me that the petitioner Amir Sultan Ali Haider acted in accordance with the direction of the Appellate Division in view of the fact that the question of appointement of Mutwalli was required to be decided by the Administrator of Waqfs in pursuance of direction of the Appellate Division and that is why, since he was holding charge of Mutwalli since 11.8.81, Amir Sultan Ali haider filed an filed an application on 11.8.85 before the Administrator of Waqf for appointment of Mutwalli. The administrator of waqf, after notifying all the parties, perusing the materials on record and hearing the parties, passed his order on 21.12.86 appointing Amir Sultan Ali Haider as Mutwalli of the said Waqf Estate on regular basis. I do not find any violation of any provision of Section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance in the aforesaid facts and circumstance of the case. The learned Additional District Judge has not seplt out as to how, where, when and why the provision of Section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance has been violated in the present case by the Waqf Administrator. The parties were in litigation for a long Amir Sultan All Haider took charge of office of the Mutalli on 11.8.81 in pursuance of the decree passed by the Court and since then he was functioning. So, the finding of the learned Additional District Judge to the effect that the provision of Section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance has been violated has no basis at all inasmuch the learned Additional District Judge has totally misconstrued the judgment of the Appellate Division as well as the material on record and thereby came to an erroneous finding to the effect that the provision of Section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance has been violated in the present case. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the material. evidence on record and my discussions above, I hold that the learned. Additional District Judge, on appeal, committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice in setting aside the order of the Administrator of Waqf dated 21.12.1986 and as such the appellate judgment is liable to be set aside.
